newsitem.title: UK: BT shares seen volatile after MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: BT shares seen volatile after MCI deal.

text.p: Shares in British Telecom are likely to be volatile on Monday after yesterday's confirmation of the company's planned acquisition of MCI Communications, traders said.
The stock, which closed at 351p on Friday before any details of the deal were known, could open up about 14p, traders said, though some said there could also be downward pressure on the stock.

Traders said news of BT's planned 35p special dividend, and enthusiasm for the industrial logic of the deal, was offset by the cost of the takeover and the dilution of the company's earnings per share by the large number of new shares it is issuing under the deal.

"Pre-opening it's anyone's guess, it could be all over the place," said one trader at a leading securities house. He said the stock could be 25p-28p higher in pre-market trade before settling back a shade at the opening.

Yesterday's $20 billion merger would create the world's second-largest telecoms group after Japan's NTT Corp. Under the terms of the deal, MCI would receive 0.54 new Amercan Depositary Shares in the new combined group and $6 cash.
